title: RC-12 dashboard "Stop chain" calls ctx.wsProvider.removeAllListeners(), which also removes the anti-rug rug-log subscription that shares the provider; "Start" only re-runs startDexListener, so anti-rug stays disarmed on that chain while the health indicator still shows connected

evidence.note: POST /:name/stop: stoppedChains.add, then ctx.wsProvider.removeAllListeners() with no event argument; the comment says the provider is kept for exit monitors
removeAllListeners() without an event stops every started subscriber and deletes every subscription tag: factory listeners, the anti-rug log filter and any in-flight V3 Mint wait alike
the anti-rug dispatcher is installed with ctx.wsProvider.on(filter, dispatcher) on the same shared provider; state.activeFilter / activeDispatcher keep pointing at the now-removed subscription
state.wsProvider and healthState = 'connected' are set at subscribe time; nothing in the stop route changes them, so the dashboard WS-health indicator keeps showing connected

onRestart: replaces the provider only if it is missing or destroyed (:1812-1821, not the case after a stop), runs a MEV health check, then startDexListener per DEX (:1836-1845); it never re-subscribes anti-rug
an in-flight V3 Mint wait listens on the same provider; it is removed too and the 30 s timeout then drops that opportunity (no buy, harmless)
the Stop dialog tells the operator: "Existing positions will continue being monitored by the exit engine." Anti-rug is not mentioned

sibling_sites_checked: Every removeAllListeners and provider re-subscription site at the base SHA (git grep -n removeAllListeners and "wsProvider.on(" over src/): chains.ts:141 (this finding, argument-less, shared provider), bot.ts:165/:172 (per-contract Mint, scoped, correct), bot.ts:2335 (shutdown, followed by destroy, correct). Re-subscription paths for the anti-rug filter: the detector subscribe path (detector.ts:643-657) runs on a new position registration and on the anti-rug reconnect (handleWsClose, detector.ts:916-944); onRestart (bot.ts:1808-1852) does neither. So after Stop the chain's held positions have no rug-log subscription until the next buy registers on that chain (Stop does not stop HTTP-polled buys, AUD-BUY-011), a WebSocket reconnect, or a bot restart; and no backfill covers the gap. The three-writer ownership problem of ctx.wsProvider (RC-13) is AUD-ANTIRUG-001, which records this same stop consequence from the anti-rug side; the DEX-listener side (duplicate listeners, no backfill, leaked providers) is AUD-BUY-008; Stop not stopping buys is AUD-BUY-011. This entry is the canonical RC-12 (H1) entry.
severity_rationale: S1 STRAND, equal to the research suggestion: one dashboard click that the UI describes as safe for open positions silently turns off the rug-pull exit for every position on that chain, and Start does not bring it back; the WS health indicator keeps showing connected, so the operator has no signal. A rug during that window is not detected (the routine stop-loss poll still runs, so not S0). The same mechanism was already shown to the operator as part of AUD-ANTIRUG-001 (ESC-ANTIRUG-01); it is presented again in the API batch as its own RC-12 item. Bot OFF, no live exposure.
recommendation: Never call an argument-less removeAllListeners on a shared provider. Under card OD-11 (one WebSocket owner per chain that notifies subscribers) Stop pauses only the chain's DEX factory subscribers by handle, anti-rug is never touched by Stop/Start, and Start resumes the same subscribers with a backfill from the last seen block. The Stop dialog text should say exactly what keeps running. Real-path test: Stop then Start a chain with a registered position and assert a rug log still reaches dispatchEvent. Phase 24 (capital), nothing changed in Phase 22.

sub_claims.claim: Stop removes the anti-rug log subscription with all other provider listeners
Start (onRestart) re-attaches only DEX listeners; anti-rug is re-subscribed only by a later position registration, a reconnect or a restart
Nothing tells the operator: health stays connected and the Stop dialog says positions keep being monitored

traces.scenario: Operator stops a WebSocket chain with one open position, later starts it again
steps: POST /api/chains/eth/stop -> removeAllListeners() on ctx.wsProvider (chains.ts:141): the anti-rug filter subscription is stopped (eth_unsubscribe) and deleted
the position keeps its 5 s exit poll (HTTP provider); anti-rug state still says 'connected' (detector.ts:678-679)
POST /api/chains/eth/start -> onRestart: provider is not destroyed, so it is kept; startDexListener per DEX re-adds factory listeners only (bot.ts:1812-1845)
an LP removal on the held token emits a log that no subscriber receives; no backfill runs for the stopped window
traces.outcome: The rug is not detected; the position is only protected by the routine stop-loss poll until a new position registers, the socket reconnects, or the bot restarts.
